answer: The cheapest real defence: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because ledge only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, meadow is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
